dns_rebinding.query_failed: DNS queries on {host} failed: addresses cannot be measured
dns_rebinding.score_clean: No non-public address in public DNS
finding.dns_rebinding.private_ip: {host} resolves to a non-public address ({addresses}): public DNS discloses the internal network. Remove these records from public DNS.
module.dns_rebinding.checks: Looks for non-public addresses (private network, loopback, link-local, 100.64/10, IPv6 ULA) in the A and AAAA records of the target, its domain and its mail servers.
module.dns_rebinding.fix:
Note in the finding each name and each non-public address (private network, loopback, link-local, `100.64.0.0/10`, IPv6 `fc00::/7`): these addresses do not belong in the public DNS.
Delete these A and AAAA records from the public DNS zone, at your DNS host or registrar.
If the name must keep working inside the network: create it in an internal DNS (internal zone or view of your DNS server, company resolver), not in the public DNS.
If the server is reachable from the Internet through a port forward (NAT): publish the public address of the router or firewall, never the machine's internal address.
If an MX points to a name that resolves to a private address: point it to the public name of your mail server or gateway, otherwise outside mail does not arrive.
Protect the internal network against rebinding: on the resolver (router, firewall, Unbound, dnsmasq), refuse public answers that contain private addresses, and have internal admin interfaces check the `Host` header (reject unexpected names).
Check with `dig +short A name.example.com` and `dig +short AAAA name.example.com`: only public addresses must appear; then run the scan again.
module.dns_rebinding.fix_snippet:
# Unbound
server:
    private-address: 10.0.0.0/8
    private-address: 172.16.0.0/12
    private-address: 192.168.0.0/16
    private-address: 169.254.0.0/16
    private-address: fd00::/8
    private-address: fe80::/10

# dnsmasq
stop-dns-rebind

# nginx
server {
    listen 80 default_server;
    server_name _;
    return 444;
}

# Bash
dig +short A intranet.example.com
dig +short AAAA intranet.example.com
module.dns_rebinding.title: Private IP exposed in DNS
module.dns_rebinding.why: An internal address published in public DNS reveals the network's addressing plan and gives a foothold for DNS rebinding attacks against browsers on the internal network.
